title: hawkbell event record
description: One NDJSON line written by hawkbell (outbox segments, local ring, stdout, hawkbell detect --ndjson). Schema version 1 (field v). Generated from internal/event by `go test ./internal/event -run TestSchema -update`; do not edit by hand. Reference: docs/EVENTS.md.

Account.description: Account is the identity the agent is signed in with, when a surface reports it (vendor OpenTelemetry does; hooks usually do not). It answers the first governance question: corporate tenant, personal account or a raw API key on a managed machine.

id.description: ID is the vendor account identifier; emitted as a keyed digest unless the privacy profile is full.

Agent.description: Agent identifies the AI agent product.

name.description: Product name from the catalog, on process-monitor and inventory records.

version.description: Version as the surface or the scan reported it.

pid.description: Process id of the agent, on process-monitor records.

surface.description: Surface is how the agent was run: cli | ide | desktop | sdk | ci | cloud.

Asset.description: Asset is one inventory record. ID is stable across scans for the same (host, kind, identity, owner, location) so downstream can upsert.

id.description: Stable across scans for the same host, kind, identity, owner and location, so downstream can upsert on it.

name.description: Name of the asset: the product, the declared server, skill or plugin, or the file.

catalog_id.description: CatalogID is the catalog entry that identified the asset ("" when unknown).

parent.description: Parent is the catalog id of the agent that owns this item (an MCP server declared in Cursor's config has Parent "cursor").

owner.description: OS user the item belongs to

running.description: True when the scan saw a process of the product running.

pid.description: The lowest pid of those processes.

sha256.description: SHA256 is the hex SHA-256 discovery computed for the asset; it changes when what discovery records about the asset changes. Discovery hashes no binaries: agents, apps, IDE and browser extensions, AI browsers and model runtimes get a digest of what the scan observed (version, install path, evidence, risk flags, telemetry), so a binary replaced in place at the same version keeps its value. CI agents carry the hash of the workflow file that names them, skills and plugin directories a folder hash, plugin files and the text files a user wrote (rules files, commands, subagents, project configuration) the hash of their content, MCP servers and hooks their definition hash. For MCP servers, hooks, rules files, subagents, commands and project configuration the privacy stage writes a keyed digest (24 hex digits) instead, or no value without a key; see the profile table in docs/EVENTS.md.

evidence.description: Evidence lists how identity was established, e.g. "package:npm", "bundle_id", "path", "process", "signature". Two independent classes are required for Confidence "high".

signer.description: Signer is the code-signing identity when verified (team id / publisher).

first_seen.description: Not set by the scanner in this release (last_seen and change are).

last_seen.description: Time of the scan that saw the asset.

change.description: How the asset differs from the previous scan: new (also when there is no previous state), changed, unchanged (written by a full scan only) or removed (gone since the previous scan, reported by a full scan).

risk_flags.description: RiskFlags are closed-vocabulary posture hints computed at scan time.

mcp.description: MCP holds normalized launch facts for a declared MCP server, so a central team can hunt for a bad package or endpoint across the fleet.

telemetry.description: Telemetry describes how well hawkbell can see this agent (agents only).

detail.description: Other facts about this kind of asset, as strings: for example project, plugin, marketplace, pinned, enabled, status or hooks_shadowed_by.

AssetKindPrefix.description: In a skeleton: a AssetKind value, a prefix of one, or empty (a skeleton writer may clip its strings).

Change.description: Change describes how an asset differs from the previous scan.

Check.description: Check is one posture check result.

id.description: rule id of the posture rule

title.description: Title of the rule or check.

severity.description: Severity of the rule or check.

agent_id.description: Catalog id of the agent the checked item belongs to.

asset_id.description: asset.id of the inventory record that failed the check.

scope.description: Scope is where a configuration item is declared.

subject.description: file path or setting key checked

expected.description: What the check requires, when it says (the scanner's file-owner check does).

actual.description: What was found: for an inventory rule, the evidence fields as name=value pairs separated by "; " (at most 512 bytes).

owner.description: Account the checked item belongs to.

Container.description: Container locates the workload when the agent runs in a container.

id.description: Container id, from the process's cgroup (process monitor) or from the container a scan looks into.

image.description: Image of the container. Not set by the collectors in this release.

name.description: Name of the container. Not set by the collectors in this release.

pod.description: Kubernetes pod name. Not set by the collectors in this release.

pod_uid.description: Kubernetes pod UID, from the cgroup path; absent outside Kubernetes.

namespace.description: Kubernetes namespace. Not set by the collectors in this release.

node.description: Kubernetes node name. Not set by the collectors in this release.

Coverage.description: Coverage is the per-agent, per-user visibility statement: which surfaces are actually delivering. "Not collected" must never read as "clean".

user.description: Account the row is about: its name, or its uid or SID when the name is unknown.

rule_id.description: Id of the rule that matched: a rule from a pack, an id the engine itself writes (HB-COV-901, HB-COV-902) or a relayed one (numbat:<id>). See docs/RULES.md.

class.description: Class is how much attention the match deserves: "signal" (counted into the session summary, not shipped by default), "finding" (shipped, no page) or "alert" (expected to be silent on ordinary developer work).

category.description: Category of the rule, for example execution.

tags.description: Tags carries framework mappings in Sigma tag style: attack.t1059.004, atlas.aml.t0051, owasp.asi05.

evidence.description: Evidence is a small redacted map of the field values that matched.

event_ids.description: EventIDs are the ids of the events that produced the match, oldest first; for sequence rules this is the chain.

flags.description: Flags are the session flags that were required and present.

response.description: Response is what the rule asks for (none | ask | block); Enforced says whether hawkbell actually returned that decision to the agent.

enforced.description: True only when hawkbell returned the response to the agent (guard mode); absent otherwise.

dedup_key.description: DedupKey groups repeats of the same finding; Count is how many matches this record stands for after suppression.

count.description: How many matches this record stands for: repeats inside rules.suppress_for are counted and carried on the next emission instead of being written again.

escalate.description: Escalate marks findings that are suspicious but not conclusive and are good candidates for a downstream LLM or human judge.

DetectionClassPrefix.description: In a skeleton: a DetectionClass value, a prefix of one, or empty (a skeleton writer may clip its strings).

id.description: Record id: UUID-shaped and starting with the record time in milliseconds, so ids sort by time. Version 7 ids are random; version 8 ids are derived from the record's natural key (StableID), so a replayed delivery, or the twin of a record from another surface, has the same id. Deduplicate deliveries on it.

ts.description: When the thing happened, as its source says: the hook's clock, the log's timestamp, the triggering record's ts for a finding, the write time for heartbeats and summaries.

emitted.description: Emitted is when the record was written for shipping, set only when that is more than a minute after TS (a laptop that was offline, a backfilled transcript). Rules with event-time lookback windows can schedule on it.

seq.description: monotonic per (Writer, stream), for gap detection downstream

dedupe.description: Dedupe is identical for every record that describes the same action, whichever surface reported it (see DedupeKey).

kind.description: Kind is the top-level class of a record and selects the output stream.

type.description: The record type within its kind.

source.description: Source is the collection method that produced a record.

fidelity.description: Fidelity says whether the record was directly observed or reconstructed.

sources.description: Sources lists every surface that corroborated this event after cross-surface correlation (for example ["hook","transcript"]).

integrity.description: Integrity says who could have altered a record before it was written. Hooks run as the monitored user, so their records are advisory until a privileged collector corroborates them; anything a Fleet policy depends on must be root-integrity.

writer.description: Writer identifies the process that wrote the record (random per process start). Seq is monotonic per Writer, and heartbeats report per-writer counts, so a consumer can prove that nothing was lost or removed.

host.description: Host identifies the endpoint. ID should equal osquery's system_info.uuid so events join to Fleet hosts.

user.description: User is the OS account the agent runs as.

agent.description: Agent identifies the AI agent product.

account.description: The identity the agent is signed in with. No collector in this release sets it; the Claude Code OpenTelemetry receiver records the organization as labels.org_id instead.

target.description: Target is what the tool call acts on, extracted and normalized.

prompt.description: Prompt summarizes a user prompt without necessarily carrying it.

outcome.description: Outcome is the result of a tool call or turn.

container.description: Container locates the workload when the agent runs in a container.

repo.description: Repo describes the source repository of the session's working directory.

privacy.description: Privacy is the tier that was applied when the record was emitted.

truncated.description: Truncated names fields whose values were cut, so truncation is never silent; the cut value itself ends in an "[TRUNCATED:<n>B]" marker (when a sink cuts target.command to fit its line cap it records the full length in Labels["target.command.len"] instead). No hash of the full value is kept: an unkeyed one would let a reader confirm guesses about the missing text.

labels.description: Facts that have no field of their own, as strings (hook_event, end_reason, rule_pack, context_for, first_seen and the others named in docs/EVENTS.md). Values pass the same redaction as every other string.

EventType.description: Event.Type: the activity types (Kind activity) and the types of the other kinds. detection.context is declared in internal/privacy. The Types table in docs/EVENTS.md says what each one means.

EventTypePrefix.description: In a skeleton: a EventType value, a prefix of one, or empty (a skeleton writer may clip its strings).

Fidelity.description: Fidelity says whether the record was directly observed or reconstructed.

FidelityPrefix.description: In a skeleton: a Fidelity value, a prefix of one, or empty (a skeleton writer may clip its strings).

Health.description: Health is the sensor heartbeat. It is deliberately content-free.

sensor_version.description: Version of the hawkbell binary that wrote the record.

uptime_s.description: Seconds since the writing pipeline started.

counters.description: Counters and gauges by name (see Counters in docs/EVENTS.md).

coverage.description: Coverage is the per-agent, per-user visibility statement: which surfaces are actually delivering. "Not collected" must never read as "clean".

rules_hash.description: SHA-256 of the loaded rule set; findings carry its first 12 hex digits as labels.rules_hash.

last_scan.description: Time of the last inventory scan. Not set by the heartbeat writer in this release.

reason.description: Reason is a closed-vocabulary code for health.error records.

Host.description: Host identifies the endpoint. ID should equal osquery's system_info.uuid so events join to Fleet hosts.

id.description: Host identifier, meant to equal osquery's system_info.uuid so that records join to Fleet hosts: host_id from the configuration, HAWKBELL_HOST_ID, the host_id file the osquery extension writes, or the hardware UUID (on Linux without one, machine-id). Empty when nothing is derivable; the heartbeat label host_id_source names the source.

name.description: Host name: HAWKBELL_HOST_NAME when it is set to a plausible name (the Kubernetes node sensor sets it to the node's name), else the kernel's host name.

Integrity.description: Integrity says who could have altered a record before it was written. Hooks run as the monitored user, so their records are advisory until a privileged collector corroborates them; anything a Fleet policy depends on must be root-integrity.

IntegrityPrefix.description: In a skeleton: a Integrity value, a prefix of one, or empty (a skeleton writer may clip its strings).

Kind.description: Kind is the top-level class of a record and selects the output stream.

KindPrefix.description: In a skeleton: a Kind value, a prefix of one, or empty (a skeleton writer may clip its strings).

MCP.description: MCP holds normalized launch facts for a declared MCP server, so a central team can hunt for a bad package or endpoint across the fleet.

command.description: executable as declared (basename unless tier is full)

runner.description: Runner is the package launcher when one is used: npx | bunx | uvx | pipx | pip | docker | podman | node | python | deno | binary.

package.description: Package the runner launches (an npm or PyPI name, an image).

version.description: Version or tag of that package, when the declaration names one.

pinned.description: Pinned is true only for an exact version or an image digest.

url_host.description: Host of the endpoint the client connects to (a remote transport, or the endpoint a stdio bridge is given).

header_keys.description: Names of the HTTP headers the declaration sets, never their values.

has_inline_secret.description: True when a credential-shaped literal is written into the declaration itself (command line, arguments, environment or header values, headers helper, OAuth client secret, or a token in the URL) rather than referenced. The value is never written.

enabled.description: Whether the client has the server switched on, when its configuration says (false for a server on its disabled list).

Outcome.description: Outcome is the result of a tool call or turn.

status.description: Status: ok | error | denied | interrupted | unknown.

error.description: Error text the agent reported, redacted; at most 256 bytes outside the full profile.

duration_ms.description: Duration of the call in milliseconds, when the surface reports it.

exit_code.description: Exit status of the command, when the surface reports it.

decision.description: Decision: allow | deny | ask, when a permission decision was observed.

pid.description: Process id. On hook records, the process that invoked the hook (the agent, or a shell it started); on process-monitor and exec records, the process itself.

name.description: Process name as the kernel reports it, which the process can set itself.

start_time.description: Start time of the process; with pid, the join key to EDR process telemetry.

ancestors.description: Ancestors is the chain of process names from parent to root.

env_markers.description: EnvMarkers are agent marker variable NAMES found in the environment (values are never emitted except session ids copied into Session).

flags.description: Flags are risky argv flags recognized by the catalog, e.g. "--dangerously-skip-permissions".

Profile.description: Profile names what leaves the endpoint.

Prompt.description: Prompt summarizes a user prompt without necessarily carrying it.

len.description: Length of the prompt in bytes; rounded up to a power of four outside the full profile (labels.len_bucketed).

sha256.description: keyed hash when a tenant key is configured

Repo.description: Repo describes the source repository of the session's working directory.

root.description: Root directory of the repository. Not set by the collectors in this release.

branch.description: Branch, when a surface reports it (Claude Code OpenTelemetry, numbat records).

Scope.description: Scope is where a configuration item is declared.

turn_id.description: Id of the current turn (a prompt and the work it caused), when the surface reports one.

cwd.description: Working directory of the session; a path under the acting user's home is written as ~/...

permission_mode.description: PermissionMode is the agent's own vocabulary, normalized to: default | plan | accept_edits | auto | dont_ask | bypass.

model.description: Model the session uses, as the agent reports it.

transcript.description: path of the session log, when known

subagent_id.description: Id of the subagent thread the record belongs to; absent on the main thread.

subagent_type.description: Type or name of that subagent, as the agent reports it.

SeverityPrefix.description: In a skeleton: a Severity value, a prefix of one, or empty (a skeleton writer may clip its strings).

Skeleton.description: Content-free stand-in written when redaction failed or a record could not be brought under the line cap. It carries only the fields the skeleton writers set (internal/sink, shrink.go: skeleton; internal/privacy, emit.go: skeleton and buildSkeleton), read from their source when this schema is generated; its truncated list contains "*" and, when the privacy stage wrote it, a label names the reason (privacy_error or line_cap). A writer may clip strings, so a vocabulary field holds a value of its vocabulary, a prefix of one, or nothing.

SkeletonAgent.description: The fields of Agent a skeleton keeps.

SkeletonAsset.description: The fields of Asset a skeleton keeps.

SkeletonCheck.description: The fields of Check a skeleton keeps.

SkeletonDetection.description: The fields of Detection a skeleton keeps.

SkeletonHealth.description: The fields of Health a skeleton keeps.

SkeletonHost.description: The fields of Host a skeleton keeps.

SkeletonSession.description: The fields of Session a skeleton keeps.

SkeletonTool.description: The fields of Tool a skeleton keeps.

SkeletonUser.description: The fields of User a skeleton keeps.

Source.description: Source is the collection method that produced a record.

SourcePrefix.description: In a skeleton: a Source value, a prefix of one, or empty (a skeleton writer may clip its strings).

Summary.description: Summary is the per-session rollup: enough to answer fleet-wide questions ("which hosts called MCP server X", "which sessions loaded skill hash Y") from a small indexed stream while raw activity stays local or in cold storage. It carries counts, classes and identifiers, never content.

started.description: ts of the session's earliest activity record.

ended.description: ts of its latest activity record, on the final summary only.

final.description: true when the session ended; false for periodic rollups

events.description: Activity records counted into the summary.

tool_calls.description: ToolCalls counts tool calls by normalized kind.

hosts.description: Hosts are distinct network hosts contacted through tools (capped).

host_classes.description: Distinct classes of the network hosts contacted.

path_classes.description: PathClasses are the distinct sensitive path classes touched.

installs.description: Installs are packages installed by the agent as "manager:name".

max_severity.description: Highest severity among detections, signals included.

surfaces.description: Surfaces that reported this session and the resulting coverage state (covered | partial | blind).

coverage.description: What the reporting surfaces amount to: covered (hooks and another surface), partial (hooks, or transcript or OpenTelemetry, alone) or blind (only the process monitor or osquery).

denied.description: tool calls denied by user, policy or guard

blocked.description: tool calls blocked by hawkbell guard mode

last_event.description: When the collector last delivered, by the sensor's clock (the arrival of its last record; for the process monitor its last self-check, for the scan the scan's time), not a time a record claims.

schema_drift.description: True when the collector met input in a shape it does not know (an agent changed its log or telemetry format).

reason.description: Why the status is not ok, as a code: for example config, kill_switch, checkpoint or procs_unreadable.

Target.description: Target is what the tool call acts on, extracted and normalized.

url.description: userinfo, query and fragment stripped unless tier is full

hosts.description: Further distinct network hosts the call refers to; host holds the first.

query.description: web search query; tiers redacted/full only

Telemetry.description: Telemetry is per-agent coverage state: which surfaces hawkbell has.

hooks.description: Hooks: managed | user | missing | modified | unsupported | disabled.

transcript.description: Transcript: tailing | found | none | relocated | disabled.

Time.description: RFC 3339 in UTC with exactly six fraction digits (TimeLayout), the form Fluent Bit's strict parser needs. Optional time fields are left out when unset. The pattern checks the range of every component, month and day together, and admits February 29 in every year; a validator that asserts format date-time also rejects it outside leap years.

kind.description: ToolKind is the cross-agent normalized class of a tool call.

use_id.description: agent's tool-call id; join key across surfaces

mcp_tool.description: Tool name on that MCP server, for kind mcp.

input_sha256.description: InputSHA256 is the hash of the canonical JSON of the tool input, so identical calls correlate without shipping content.

input_keys.description: InputKeys lists top-level argument names (metadata tier).

input.description: Input is the redacted tool input; present only in tiers redacted/full.

output.description: Output is the redacted, truncated tool output; tiers redacted/full only.

output_sha256.description: Keyed digest of the tool output (HMAC with the tenant key); absent without a key.

output_len.description: Size of the tool output in bytes; rounded up to a power of four outside the full profile.

ToolKind.description: ToolKind is the cross-agent normalized class of a tool call.

ToolKindPrefix.description: In a skeleton: a ToolKind value, a prefix of one, or empty (a skeleton writer may clip its strings).

User.description: User is the OS account the agent runs as.

name.description: Account name. With privacy.pseudonymize_users, a keyed pseudonym (removed when no key is configured).

id.description: uid on POSIX, SID on Windows
